newsitem.title: USA: Alleged Versace killer Cunanan believed dead.
newsitem.headline: Alleged Versace killer Cunanan believed dead.

text.p: Andrew Cunanan, the alleged killer of fashion designer Gianni Versace and four other men, appeared to have taken his own life on Wednesday after police cornered him in a houseboat on Miami Beach, authorities said.
Although officials gave no final confirmation, Miami Beach Mayor Seymour Gelber said police had told him they believed the dead man was Cunanan.
"That is the information I have received, but they have not given us final word on it," Gelber said. "The general feeling ... is that this very well may be Cunanan."
Miami Beach Police Chief Richard Barreto told a news conference that the body of a white man who bore a "similarity" to Cunanan was found inside the houseboat.

Local radio station WINZ said a .40-caliber pistol was also been found inside the residence, located between the site of Versace's murder and the hotel where Cunanan stayed for several weeks before the killing.
The FBI said on Tuesday that such a gun was used to kill Versace and two of the other four men Cunanan was accused of murdering.
Barreto said forensic tests were being carried out to confirm the dead man's identity.
Miami Beach police spokesman Al Boza said the body had a gunshot wound and that police did not fire any shots while storming the houseboat earlier on Wednesday.
Boza had earlier said the houseboat was found empty after an initial search. The body appeared to have been discovered during a second more thorough search.

Dozens of police including heavily armed SWAT assault specialists surrounded the houseboat after its caretaker reported a man resembling Cunanan had fired a shot when he approached the site around 4 p.m. EDT (2000 GMT).
Four hours later, police fired tear gas into the houseboat and then entered the two-level dwelling. They met no response and could later be seen leaving in a relaxed manner.
The siege sparked a frenzy among local media. Television stations carried live images of the site for several hours, although they respected a police request to delay broadcasting the assault itself.
Local television said the owner of the boat was identified as a German citizen who also owns a gay health club in Las Vegas. Police described Cunanan as a homosexual prostitute.

Versace, who dressed the world's beautiful people in flamboyant and sexy couture, was shot and killed on July 15 at the gate of his oceanfront mansion in the trendy Art Deco South Beach area of Miami Beach.
Versace was also a homosexual but there was no confirmation the two men had a relationship.

Variously described as a gay prostitute down on his luck and a charming, intelligent chameleon who could change his appearance at will, Cunanan blurred the lines between the usual categories applied to multiple murderers, experts in the field said.

They said Cunanan began as a "spree killer" set off by a desire for vengeance against a known victim, then developed a taste for cruelty shared by serial killers, and finally sought the infamy perceived by mass murderers.
Police said they believed he could have disguised himself as a woman to try to elude police during the nine-day manhunt he sparked.
He was also wanted for the murders of his former lover Jeffrey Trail, 28, in late April; their mutual friend David Madson, 33, in May; Lee Miglin, 72, also in May; and William Reese, 45, also in May.
